---
title: Content
---

What a TEXT File shows is a Message: one or more Frames, shown one after
another. Each Frame has a Mode, a Display Position, and its content. The
content is a list of Segments: strings of literal text, and Control Codes
that change how the text after them looks or insert a live value.

```python
from alpha_led_sign import Color, CurrentTime, Frame, Message, Mode, Position

message = Message(
    Frame(Mode.ROTATE, Position.TOP, [Color.RED, "Doors open at 7"]),
    Frame(Mode.HOLD, Position.BOTTOM, [Color.GREEN, CurrentTime()]),
)
sign.write_text("A", message)
```

The same Message can be written as [markup](03-markup.qmd):

```python
sign.write_text("A", "{frame rotate top}{color red}Doors open at 7"
                     "{frame hold bottom}{color green}{time}")
```

Use whichever reads better. Markup is shorter for fixed text. Segments are safer
for text from outside the program, because a string in a list of Segments is
always literal.

## Modes

The Mode says how a Frame comes onto the display: `Mode.ROTATE` moves it across,
`Mode.HOLD` keeps it still, and `Mode.FLASH` flashes it. The `ROLL_*` and `WIPE_*`
Modes replace the old text in the direction their name gives. `Mode.AUTOMODE` lets
the Sign choose.

Two more enums add Modes the manual lists separately:

- `SpecialMode`: effects such as `TWINKLE`, `SNOW`, `SPARKLE`, `SLIDE`, and the
  `WELCOME` and `SLOT_MACHINE` animations.
- `SpecialGraphic`: built-in animations such as `FIREWORKS` and `THANK_YOU`. A
  Frame with a Special Graphic can't show text, so put the text in the next Frame.

```python
from alpha_led_sign import SpecialGraphic, SpecialMode

Message(
    Frame(SpecialGraphic.FIREWORKS),
    Frame(SpecialMode.SNOW, Position.FILL, ["Happy new year"]),
)
```

`Mode.EXPLODE` and `Mode.CLOCK` need Alpha 3.0, which the 4000 Series does not
have. The library warns before it sends them to a model that lacks them.

## Display Positions

A two-line Sign such as the 4120C shows a Frame on `Position.TOP`,
`Position.BOTTOM`, `Position.MIDDLE`, or `Position.FILL` (the default). On a
one-line Sign every position shows on the one line.

Fonts taller than 7 rows (`Font.TEN_HIGH`, `Font.FULL_HEIGHT`, and
`Font.FULL_HEIGHT_FANCY`) show at full height only in `Position.MIDDLE`. In the
other positions a two-line Sign draws them 7 rows high, and the library warns:

```python
sign.show("{font full_height}BIG", position=Position.MIDDLE)
```

## Control Codes

A Control Code applies to the text after it, until another Control Code of the
same kind replaces it.

| To change | Use | Markup |
|---|---|---|
| Color | `Color.RED`, `Color.AMBER`, `Color.RAINBOW_1`, ... | `{color red}` |
| Font | `Font.SEVEN_HIGH`, `Font.FIVE_HIGH`, ... | `{font seven_high}` |
| Speed | `Speed.SPEED_1` (slowest) to `Speed.SPEED_5` | `{speed 1}` |
| Character width | `Wide()`, `Wide(False)` | `{wide on}`, `{wide off}` |
| Flashing | `CharacterFlash()` | `{flash on}` |
| Spacing | `Spacing.FIXED_WIDTH`, `Spacing.PROPORTIONAL` | `{spacing fixed_width}` |
| Other attributes | `CharacterAttribute(Attribute.FANCY, True)` | `{attribute fancy on}` |
| Line break | `Control.NEW_LINE` | `{new_line}` |

Literal text must be printable ASCII. A newline in a string is an error; use
`Control.NEW_LINE` instead.

These insert a value the Sign keeps up to date:

| Shows | Use | Markup |
|---|---|---|
| The time | `CurrentTime()` | `{time}` |
| The date | `CurrentDate(DateFormat.MMM_DD_YYYY)` | `{date mmm_dd_yyyy}` |
| A STRING File's content | `StringRef("T")` | `{string T}` |
| A DOTS PICTURE File | `DotsPictureRef("P")` | `{picture P}` |

The time and date come from the Sign's own clock; see
[Scheduling, clock, and sound](06-scheduling-clock-sound.qmd). STRING Files are
the way to show values that change; see [Files and memory](04-files-and-memory.qmd).

Not every Sign Model has every Control Code. A red-only "R" model has no colors,
and the 4000 Series has no double-height characters or new pages. The library
warns before it sends one of those to a model that lacks it.

## Shortcuts

`Sign.show` builds a one-Frame Message for you and writes it to TEXT File `A`:

```python
sign.show("Hello")
sign.show("Hello", mode=Mode.ROTATE, position=Position.TOP)
sign.show([Color.AMBER, "Hello"])
```

Pass `label=` to write a TEXT File other than `A`. That File must exist in the
Memory Configuration first.

`Sign.write_text` takes a Message, a single Frame, or markup.

## Reading content back

`Sign.read_text` returns the Message a TEXT File holds, and `to_markup` writes it
as markup:

```python
from alpha_led_sign import to_markup

print(to_markup(sign.read_text("A")))
# {frame rotate top}{color red}Doors open at 7{frame hold bottom}{color green}{time}
```

A Control Code the library does not model comes back as a `RawControl` with its
bytes, written `{raw ...}` in markup, so the content can be written back unchanged.
